title: Aggrega Wasm Parser Socket
description: The JSON wire shapes a parser plugin socket consumes (ParseInput) and emits (ParseOutput). A parser is a stateless, side-effect-free transformer that turns a foreign text representation into a canonical structured JSON tree, so any consumer in any language can read the tree without carrying its own language parser. A parser declares the formats it handles as parse:<format> capabilities in its descriptor; the host hands it the bytes to parse and the format name, and it returns the tree plus optional diagnostics and source spans. The parser attaches no meaning to the tree beyond its syntax — the compiler pipes the tree through opaquely.

ParseInput.description: The payload a parser guest receives: the format name that selects how to read the bytes, the source bytes to parse, and an optional opaque options document the consumer supplies for parser-specific behavior.

format.description: The name of the source format to parse, matching one of the parser's advertised parse:<format> capabilities (for example hcl, toml, yaml, or json). The parser reads the bytes as this format.

bytes.description: The source bytes to parse, base64-encoded on the wire. The parser decodes the base64 to recover the original bytes and reads them as the named format.

options.description: An opaque options document the consumer supplies for parser-specific behavior. The host pipes it through without interpreting it; the parser reads whatever shape it documents. Absent when the consumer supplies no options.

ParseOutput.description: The payload a parser guest returns: the canonical structured tree of the parsed source, plus any diagnostics the parse raised and any source spans locating tree nodes back to the original bytes.

tree.description: The canonical structured view of the parsed source, as a JSON document. The top level may be an object, an array, or a scalar, matching the parsed document's own shape (a JSON file, for example, may parse to any of these). The host pipes the tree through opaquely, carrying it verbatim without interpreting its content.

diagnostics.description: Diagnostics the parse raised — for example a syntax error or a warning. Absent when the parse produced none.

spans.description: Source spans locating tree nodes back to their position in the original bytes, so a consumer can map a finding on a tree node to a source location. Absent when the parser reports no spans.

ParseDiagnostic.description: One diagnostic the parse raised: a severity, a human-readable message, and an optional source span locating the diagnostic in the original bytes.

severity.description: The diagnostic's severity — for example error or warning. An open string so a parser can report its own severity vocabulary.

span.description: The source span locating the diagnostic in the original bytes. Absent when the parser attaches no location to the diagnostic.

NodeSpan.description: A source span for one tree node: an RFC 6901 JSON Pointer addressing the node within the tree, paired with the span locating it in the original bytes.

pointer.description: An RFC 6901 JSON Pointer into the tree, addressing the node this span locates.

span.description: The span locating the addressed node in the original bytes.

SourceSpan.description: A span of the original source bytes: the byte offsets are the primary, exact location, and the line and column numbers accompany them for human-readable diagnostics.

start_offset.description: The byte offset of the span's first byte in the original source, zero-based.

end_offset.description: The byte offset one past the span's last byte in the original source, so end_offset minus start_offset is the span's length in bytes.

start_line.description: The line number of the span's start, one-based, for human-readable diagnostics.

start_column.description: The column number of the span's start, one-based, for human-readable diagnostics.

end_line.description: The line number of the span's end, one-based, for human-readable diagnostics.

end_column.description: The column number of the span's end, one-based, for human-readable diagnostics.

ParseSourceResponse.description: The parse-source host function's reply: on success the canonical structured tree the resolved parser produced, on failure an error message. Exactly one of the two fields is populated. Failure is delivered in-band rather than by trapping, so a consumer guest carries a no-parser or a parse failure into its own diagnostics as a deterministic failure. This is the envelope a consumer socket receives when it asks the host to run a producer through the host; the request payload is a ParseInput.

tree.description: The canonical structured tree the resolved parser produced on success, as a JSON document carried verbatim; absent on failure.

error.description: The failure message on failure, naming the format and the reason; absent on success.
